claims.claim: Cua announced 'Computer History' for Cua Driver, an encrypted local action-history log, via a 9-tweet thread from @trycua
Computer History is an off-by-default feature gated behind the Cua Driver 'nightly' release channel, not GA/stable
Default retention period for Computer History is 7 days
Default encrypted-store quota for Computer History is 100 MiB, capping queries at 200 metadata events

Each history record is encrypted/authenticated as a COSE_Encrypt0 record via ChaCha20-Poly1305, keyed by per-chunk HKDF derivation off a namespace root key stored in the OS credential store, with no plaintext fallback and no network I/O
History records are framed as a CBOR Sequence per RFC 8742, with CloudEvents 1.0 JSON as the plaintext schema inside each encrypted payload

Computer History explicitly never stores screenshots, video, audio, typed text, raw keystrokes, clipboard contents, raw tool arguments/results, accessibility trees, file paths, window titles, URLs, or free-form diagnostics
Encryption keys are stored via macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service, and the Linux path fails closed if no unlocked Secret Service implementation is running

Agents get only two read-only, permission-gated tools (history_status, history_query); they cannot enable, pause, disable, delete, export, or access the encryption key, and a successful non-empty query itself appends an encrypted access-audit record
Cua (legal entity Cua AI, Inc.) was part of Y Combinator's Spring 2025 (X25) batch as a 2-3 person team founded by Francesco Bonacci and Alessandro Puppo
Cua reportedly raised approximately $500,000 in a pre-seed/seed round around mid-2025
The trycua/cua GitHub repository has 21,702 stars, 1,485 forks, and 679 open issues, MIT-licensed, created 2025-01-31
trycua/cua has shipped 500+ tagged releases across components since May 2025, including automated nightly builds
Cua's Python package cua-computer received roughly 435,000 PyPI downloads in the trailing month
No major tech-press coverage (TechCrunch, VentureBeat, The Information) of Cua/trycua was found as of this research
Anthropic first shipped 'computer use' in public beta alongside an upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet on October 22, 2024

Anthropic's memory tool shipped in public beta September 29, 2025; it stores files entirely in infrastructure the calling application controls, not on Anthropic's servers, and contains no automatic action/audit trail of computer-use actions

Anthropic's context editing clears stale tool-call results within one long-running session (server-side, triggered at 100,000 input tokens by default); it addresses within-session context growth, not cross-session recovery, which is a different problem from Cua's Computer History

Anthropic's internal benchmark on a 100-turn web-search agentic task found memory tool + context editing combined produced an 84% token-consumption reduction and 39% performance improvement over baseline

OpenAI's and Google's computer-use APIs (the 'computer' tool and Gemini Computer Use) are stateless per call — the developer's own harness must resend screenshots and prior context each turn; neither vendor documents a persistent, vendor-maintained cross-session action-history store

OpenAI shipped its own, identically-named 'Computer History' feature in the ChatGPT Mac desktop app on August 13, 2026 (five days before Cua) — it records macOS accessibility events locally for up to 48 hours, then sends them to OpenAI's servers to generate memory files that are saved back to disk as unencrypted plain-text Markdown
RFC 8742 defines CBOR Sequences as the concatenation of zero or more encoded CBOR data items, purpose-built for appendable, streamable data — a reasonable fit for an append-only local log

RFC 9052 defines COSE_Encrypt0 as the correct minimal structure for single-recipient encryption with an implicitly-known key, distinct from COSE_Encrypt which carries a recipients array for multi-party key distribution

CloudEvents 1.0 is a CNCF-graduated specification (January 2024) whose stated purpose is interoperability of event data across different services, platforms, and systems — a purpose that does not clearly apply to a payload encrypted with a single implicit local key that never leaves the machine
RFC 8439's security considerations name nonce uniqueness as the single most important implementation requirement for ChaCha20-Poly1305, since nonce reuse leaks the XOR of two plaintexts

OpenAdapt.AI, an MIT-licensed open-source project with copyright coverage since 2023, is local-first by design (recording, compilation, and replay run entirely on the operator machine) and offers optional AES-256-GCM encryption at rest for compiled bundles and durable checkpoints — though raw recordings and run reports are explicitly unencrypted by default

Cua's own technical documentation (README and Computer History preview doc) makes no 'first-of-its-kind' or priority claim; the 'first open-source Computer History' framing appears only in a founder's LinkedIn announcement post
The EU AI Act requires high-risk AI systems to support automatic event logging (Article 12), with deployers obligated under Articles 19/26 to retain those logs for a minimum of six months

In Camunda's 2026 enterprise survey, 71% of organizations report using AI agents but only 11% of agentic AI use cases reached production in the prior year, with 84% citing business risk and 66% citing compliance concerns
SOC 2 has no AI-specific trust-services criteria as of 2026; auditors instead apply existing CC6 (access control) and CC7 (system operations/monitoring) criteria to AI agent action logs
